accepted.question_text: For integers p, q, k with p >= q >= k + 1, Matousek's theorem states that there is a constant c(p,q,k) such that every k-uniform hypergraph satisfying the (p,q)-property has transversal number at most c(p,q,k). Is it possible to choose this bound with asymptotic growth c(p,q,k) = O(p^k)?

evidence.quote: Theorem 2 (Matousek [10]). For any integers p ≥ q ≥ k + 1, there is a constant c = c(p,q,k) such that for any k-uniform hypergraph satisfying the (p,q)-property, τ (H) ≤ c(p,q,k).
It is open whether c(p,q,k) can be taken to be O(pk). This seems hard even for the case q = k + 1.

accepted.question_text: For integers p, q, k with p >= q >= k >= 2, a dense-hypergraph (p,q)-theorem gives a bounded transversal number under an explicit density assumption (for example, requiring at least x n^k edges, equivalently a fixed positive edge-density level). Can this density requirement be strictly weakened, or removed entirely, while still guaranteeing a bounded transversal number from the (p,q)-property?

evidence.quote: Theorem 3. For any integers p ≥ q ≥ k ≥ 2 and any x > 0, there exists t = t(p,q,k,x) such that for any k-uniform hypergraph H satisfying the (p,q)-property and with at least xnk edges, τ (H) < t.
The question whether the density requirement can be reduced, maybe even removed, remains open.

accepted.question_text: For fixed integers k and p, does there exist a constant c = c(k,p) such that every k-uniform hypergraph in which every set of p edges has nonempty common intersection (that is, the (p,p)-property) has transversal number strictly less than c?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 14 (Erdos). For any fixed k and p, there exists a constant c such that for every k-uniform hypergraph H that satisfies the (p,p)-property, τ (H) < c.
It is a central conjecture of Erdos that for any fixed k and p there is a constant c such that if every set of p edges in a k-uniform hypergraph intersects, then it has a transversal of size c.
